passage: During the class picnic I watched Akash tease Jahnavi about her lunchbox: “Hey, Rice Queen!” The first time she laughed and threw a grape at him. The second time she smiled, but a bit less. The third time he said it louder, and other boys joined in. Jahnavi stopped eating. She looked at the ground and went quiet. Akash noticed and said, “I was just joking.” I couldn't tell whether he meant harm. But Jahnavi's face was different from the first time, and it was three against one. I went and told Miss Reddy what I saw, quietly, at the end of lunch.

qa.q: What did Akash call Jahnavi?
qa.a: “Rice Queen.”

qa.q: What might Jahnavi have been feeling by the third tease, and what shows it?
qa.a: She laughed at first, but by the third tease she stopped eating and looked at the ground, so it seemed the teasing no longer felt like fun and she may have felt hurt.

qa.q: What did the observer do about it?
qa.a: The observer quietly told Miss Reddy what was seen, since it was repeated and three against one.

qa.q: How might Akash have seen his own teasing?
qa.a: He may have meant it as a joke, and he said so, but he may not have noticed how it landed until Jahnavi went quiet.

grounding: Teasing among friends can shift into mocking when one person cannot laugh along, and watching the target's face and repetition helps tell fun from unkind.

passage:
Monday. At lunch Jagdish called Preeti “Slowcoach” because she was last in the race. She laughed and said, “Watch out, I'll beat you next time.”

Wednesday. He said it again in front of the whole line. Preeti smiled thinly and didn't reply. A friend, Mira, glanced at her.

Friday. Jagdish said it a third time, louder, and others joined. Preeti's face went blank, and she walked away. Mira followed her, then said to Jagdish, “She's not laughing anymore.” Jagdish stopped. He looked at Preeti's back. “I didn't mean it that way,” he said. Mira told the teacher about the three days.

qa.q: How many days in the week did Jagdish tease Preeti?
qa.a: Three, on Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

qa.q: What was Preeti feeling on Friday when her face went blank, and how was that different from Monday?
qa.a: On Monday she laughed, but by Friday she went blank and walked away, which suggests she was hurt and no longer found it funny.

qa.q: What did Mira do that helped?
qa.a: Mira followed Preeti, told Jagdish that Preeti was not laughing anymore and told the teacher about the three days.

qa.q: How might Jagdish feel after he stopped?
qa.a: He may feel surprised and a little ashamed, since he said he did not mean it that way.

grounding: Playful teasing became mocking when Preeti could not laugh along, across three days, and an adult was told about ongoing harm.

passage: Ganga, you and your friends call Minu “Tiny”, and you say she laughs. Let your Hafsa Nani tell you about Zohra. When I was ten, I called my friend Zohra “Owl” because of her big round glasses. She laughed, the first time. She even hooted back. Then the older girls heard, and every day at the pump they hooted at her, all together, flapping their arms. Zohra stopped laughing. She started walking the long way round. I told myself it was only a joke, because it had started as one. One morning I saw her face at the pump, stiff and wet. I went straight to our teacher, and she stopped it that day. Watch the face, Ganga. Not the first laugh. The face after.

qa.q: Why did young Hafsa call Zohra “Owl”?
qa.a: Because of Zohra's big round glasses.

qa.q: What was Zohra feeling when the older girls hooted at her every day?
qa.a: Zohra felt hurt and humiliated, so much that she stopped laughing and walked the long way round.

qa.q: What choice did young Hafsa make, and why did it matter?
qa.a: She went straight to the teacher when she saw Zohra's stiff, wet face, and the teacher stopped the mocking that day.

qa.q: How did the teasing change once the older girls joined in?
qa.a: It turned from a shared joke between friends into daily group mocking by older girls, which Zohra couldn't laugh along with.

grounding: Shows playful teasing turning into mocking through repetition and a power imbalance, and a child telling an adult about the ongoing harm.

passage: It was nearly ten at night, and the class group chat was exploding. Someone had posted a photo of Ramesh's new haircut with a bowl drawn on top, and the laughing faces kept coming. Sachin had sent one too, at first. It had seemed like the usual teasing; Ramesh always joked back. Not tonight. Ramesh hadn't typed anything for twenty minutes, though the chat showed he'd seen every message. Sachin's stomach turned. Four people had joined in, and it wasn't stopping. He deleted his own reaction and typed, “Okay, enough, not funny anymore.” Then he messaged Ramesh privately: “You okay? Sorry I laughed.” Then he went to his mother, still up, and showed her. She took a screenshot and emailed the class teacher that night.

qa.q: What had been drawn on Ramesh's haircut photo?
qa.a: A bowl had been drawn on top.

qa.q: What was Sachin feeling when Ramesh stayed silent?
qa.a: Sachin felt uneasy and guilty, his stomach turning as he realised the teasing had become mocking.

qa.q: What steps did Sachin take once he saw it had gone too far?
qa.a: He deleted his reaction, told the group to stop, messaged Ramesh privately to apologise and showed his mother, who emailed the teacher that night.

qa.q: What might the silence mean for Ramesh?
qa.a: Ramesh had seen every message but said nothing, which suggests he was hurt and couldn't laugh along.

grounding: Shows teasing in a group chat turning into mocking when the target goes silent and more people join, and a child telling an adult the same night.

passage: In the Delhi colony's community room, Gurleen had been teasing little Ramesh all afternoon about losing at carrom. “Butterfingers! Even my Nani plays better!” At first he giggled and stuck his tongue out. Gurleen was two years older and the colony champion, and the older kids laughed every time she said it. By the fourth game, Ramesh wasn't giggling. His chin was down, and he flicked the striker without looking. When he missed again and Gurleen opened her mouth, she stopped. His eyes were wet. She put down her striker. “Hey. I've been going on too long. Sorry. Want me to show you the angle shot?” Ramesh sniffed and nodded.

qa.q: Who was the colony carrom champion?
qa.a: Gurleen was the colony champion.

qa.q: What was Ramesh feeling by the fourth game?
qa.a: Ramesh felt hurt and embarrassed, his chin down and eyes wet from the repeated teasing.

qa.q: What did Gurleen notice, and what did she do about it?
qa.a: She noticed his lowered chin and wet eyes, stopped teasing, apologised and offered to teach him the angle shot.

qa.q: Why was the teasing harder for Ramesh to laugh off?
qa.a: Gurleen was older and the champion, and the older kids kept laughing, so the teasing had an unequal power balance and kept repeating.

grounding: Shows playful teasing turning into mocking through repetition and a power imbalance, and a child noticing the target's face and stopping.

passage:
"Oye, Professor Wasim! Those new glasses can see the moon from here!" Tarun grinned, tossing the tennis ball.
Wasim pushed the frames up and laughed. "At least I can see your wides, bowler."
"Professor, professor!" chanted Ravi and Kunal from the other end of the lane.
"Okay, okay." Wasim's laugh came out shorter.
"Professor, read the scoreboard with your telescope!" Ravi called again.
Wasim didn't answer. He stared at the ground and missed an easy ball.
Tarun walked up. "You've gone quiet."
"It was funny once," Wasim said. "Not five times. And it's three of you and one of me."
Tarun turned round. "Enough, yaar. Joke's over."
"We were only joking," Kunal said.
"He isn't laughing," Tarun said. "That's how you know." He tossed Wasim the ball. "Sorry. Your bowl."
Wasim half smiled. "Watch out, then."

qa.q: What did Ravi and Kunal chant from the other end of the lane?
qa.a: They chanted "Professor, professor!"

qa.q: What was Wasim feeling once his laugh came out shorter?
qa.a: His laugh came out shorter, he went quiet and missed an easy ball. He enjoyed it at first, but felt hurt and outnumbered once it was repeated by three boys.

qa.q: What did Tarun do that turned things around?
qa.a: He watched Wasim's face rather than the others' laughter, told the group the joke was over, and said sorry.

qa.q: Why might Kunal see the teasing differently from Wasim?
qa.a: Kunal was on the joking side, so it felt harmless to him; Wasim was alone against three, so the same words stung.

grounding: It illustrates playful teasing between friends sliding into mocking when it is repeated and one-sided, and a friend reading the target's face to stop it.
